title: Microsoft Purview: delete inactive OneDrives and mailboxes for departed users (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap targets and distinguishes existing cleanup controls from the planned capability. The controls and licensing background are supported; cite the government-cloud roadmap entry and clarify that a newly created cleanup policy can initially be left off.

claims.claim: The Purview service description lists Priority cleanup policy usage licences beginning with Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5.
claims.quote:
To use the Priority cleanup policy to apply labels that bypass existing retention or eDiscovery holds, the following licenses provide user rights:
- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A user's OneDrive site cannot be deleted while its Preservation Hold library has items with unexpired retention periods.
claims.quote: When one or more items in a Preservation Hold library have an unexpired retention period, the OneDrive site for the user can't be deleted.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An inactive mailbox can be permanently deleted by removing all its holds.
claims.quote: When you no longer need to keep the contents of an inactive mailbox, you can permanently delete the mailbox by removing all holds on it.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup cannot be used for items marked as records or regulatory records.
claims.quote: You can't use priority cleanup for items that are marked as a record or regulatory record.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup cannot delete data already copied to an eDiscovery review set.
claims.quote: Although priority cleanup can override eDiscovery holds, the data might already be copied to an eDiscovery review set where it can't be deleted by priority cleanup.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Managing SharePoint and OneDrive priority cleanup, including its tenant switch, requires the Priority Cleanup Admin role.
claims.quote: you must have the Priority Cleanup Admin role. For SharePoint and OneDrive, this role is required to create and manage priority cleanup policies, and enable or disable the feature.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive priority cleanup requires approval by at least one person besides the policy creator.
claims.quote: each item subject to priority cleanup always requires at least one other person to approve the deletion in addition to the person who created the priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive priority cleanup must run in simulation at least once.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, you must run simulation at least one time, and for any change other than the policy description.

claims.claim: An inactive mailbox becomes eligible for permanent deletion after a 30-day soft-deleted retention period following removal of its final hold.
claims.quote: if you remove the final hold from an inactive mailbox the mailbox will be permanently deleted after the 30-day soft-deleted mailbox retention period expires.

claims.claim: A permanently deleted inactive mailbox cannot be recovered.
claims.quote: After the inactive mailbox is permanently deleted, it can't be recovered.

claims.claim: The tenant priority cleanup switch is at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup settings > Configuration > control for priority cleanup.
claims.quote:
Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management.
2. From the top right, select Priority cleanup settings.
3. From the Configuration page, turn off the control for priority cleanup, and select Save.

claims.claim: An automation operation for the tenant priority cleanup availability switch is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview priority cleanup tenant configuration disable PowerShell Set PriorityCleanup enabled; "priority cleanup" "Set-PolicyConfig" tenant enable disable; read both cleanup pages and searched all Set-PolicyConfig parameter names; no tenant-switch operation.

claims.claim: The tenant priority cleanup switch applies to Exchange, SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: When you turn off priority cleanup, you're turning it off for Exchange as well as for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Existing priority cleanup is enabled by default at the tenant level.
claims.quote: Because of the built-in safeguards, the feature itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.

claims.claim: Turning off the tenant switch prevents creation of new priority cleanup policies.
claims.quote: New priority cleanup policies can't be created until you turn on the control and select Save again.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing priority cleanup policies continue to function when the tenant switch is off.
claims.quote:
If priority cleanup policies are already created when you turn off the control:
- Existing priority cleanup policies continue to function

claims.claim: Existing priority cleanup policies can be deleted when the tenant switch is off.
claims.quote: Existing priority cleanup policies can be deleted

claims.claim: Existing priority cleanup policies cannot be modified when the tenant switch is off.
claims.quote: Existing priority cleanup policies can't be modified

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > + Create a priority cleanup opens the policy creation wizard.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup, and then select + Create a priority cleanup.

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -PriorityCleanup creates a priority cleanup policy in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. The Name parameter specifies the unique name of the retention policy. The PriorityCleanup switch specifies whether to create a Priority cleanup policy. You don't need to specify a value with this switch.

claims.claim: The wizard configures the OneDrive location.
claims.quote: For Static scope, select Policy for SharePoint/OneDrive and then select one or more of the locations for sites and OneDrive accounts.

claims.claim: The wizard configures a query to target specific files.
claims.quote: For the Tell us what you're looking for page, enter text into the KeyQL editor box to construct a query to target specific files.

claims.claim: The wizard configures approvers.
claims.quote: For the Assign who'll approve what gets deleted page, this is where you need to specify an approver for when an identified item has one or more eDiscovery holds applied:

claims.claim: The initial SharePoint and OneDrive priority cleanup policy runs in simulation.
claims.quote: For the Choose the policy mode page, choose whether to run the policy first in simulation mode or leave it turned off. Running the policy in simulation mode is required to initially set up priority cleanup for SharePoint and OneDrive locations.
claims.fix: Replace 'the initial policy runs in simulation' in controls[1].note with 'the policy can initially run in simulation or remain off; simulation is required before it is turned on'. This preserves the required first-run safeguard without implying that creation always starts a run.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive priority cleanup requires a second priority cleanup administrator in the configuration flow.
claims.quote: Another priority cleanup admin is included in the policy configuration flow before the policy is turned on

claims.claim: The documented procedure for excluding an inactive mailbox from older organization-wide retention holds has no admin-centre UI equivalent.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview inactive mailbox remove retention policy hold admin center UI ExcludeFromAllOrgHolds; read Delete an inactive mailbox and returned excerpts. Its instructions require Exchange Online PowerShell, not EAC or Purview, for these procedures.

claims.claim: Set-Mailbox <identity of inactive mailbox> -ExcludeFromAllOrgHolds in Exchange Online PowerShell removes organization-wide retention policy holds using older retention locations.
claims.quote:
For retention policies that use the older retention locations, such as Exchange mailboxes, Teams chats and Copilot interactions, and Teams channel messages:
Set-Mailbox <identity of inactive mailbox> -ExcludeFromAllOrgHolds

claims.claim: An inactive mailbox cannot be removed from a retention policy with Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: You won't be able to remove an inactive mailbox if the retention policy has Preservation Lock applied.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity enables auditing when it is off.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity. Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true enables organization auditing.
claims.quote:
Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing.
Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup requires auditing enabled at least one day before the first policy is created and run.
claims.quote: Make sure that auditing is enabled at least one day before you create and run the first priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: PriorityCleanupFileRecycled is the audit operation for deletion of a SharePoint or OneDrive item by priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Operation name of PriorityCleanupFileRecycled: The deletion of an item in SharePoint or OneDrive by priority cleanup.

claims.claim: Exchange mailbox priority cleanup is rolling out in preview and subject to change.
claims.quote: Priority cleanup is rolling out in preview and subject to change.

claims.claim: The existing control rows are not documented as controls for the new roadmap capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview delete inactive OneDrives mailboxes departed users containers 566527 default licensing safeguards; read priority cleanup, mailbox deletion and auditing pages; none identifies its controls as governing this planned combined content-and-container capability.
